chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Harun ibn Muslim, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What do you say regarding a man who made the matter of his wife to be in her hands?' So he said: 'He has given the matter to the one who is not deserving of it, and he has opposed the Sunnah, and the marriage is not allowed'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband giving his wife the authority to decide their marital status?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal implications of a husband delegating marital authority to his wife, ruling that such delegation constitutes a deviation from the Prophetic Sunnah if the wife is not deemed fully appropriate to exercise independent judgment. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while *takhliq* (granting choice) is valid, it must align with the structural integrity of the marriage contract to ensure the wife’s decision carries the weight of a proper divorce or retention. The ruling underscores the importance of adhering to established marital protocols rather than arbitrary delegation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from haroun Bin Muslim, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a man who made the matter of his wife to be in her hands?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He has given the matter to the one who is not deserving of it, and he has opposed the Sunnah, and the marriage is not allowed’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Harun ibn Muslim from certain persons of our people who have said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who leaves the affairs of his wife in her own hands. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has given the matter in the hands of someone who is not proper for it, thus, he has opposed the Sunnah and has not made marriage permissible.’”
